lessons.title: Use remote controls, trusted functions, and presence
lessons.summary: Apply safe Remote Config defaults, distinguish App Check from authorization, design idempotent callable work, and choose Realtime Database for presence.
objectives: Validate Remote Config values before activating product behavior.
Explain the different questions answered by Auth, App Check, rules and trusted code.
Design a recoverable callable cleanup command with stable identity.
Use connection-aware presence without claiming it is proof of attention.

sections.title: Give every control one clear responsibility
sections.html:
Remote Config distributes product parameters. App Check supplies evidence about the calling app environment. Authentication supplies user identity. A callable Function runs trusted server code. They are complementary tools, not four ways to grant the same permission. Decide which question each mechanism is allowed to answer.

Use the notebook as the concrete example. Remote Config can propose notes_page_size. App Check can help protect the backend from unauthorized client environments. Auth identifies Alice. Security rules let Alice edit her notes. A trusted Function can accept Alice's request to clean up one owned media object.

A remote parameter must not contain a secret or grant administrative rights. A downloaded flag is visible to a client and can be modified by a modified client. If a feature needs a paid entitlement or restricted resource, the server still verifies that entitlement on the protected operation.

Android engineers may know Remote Config and Play Integrity. On Apple platforms the App Attest/DeviceCheck provider choices and integration differ. The product's desired trust boundary can be analogous while the evidence sources, deployment requirements and failure behavior are platform-specific.

sections.title: Keep a usable default and validate the proposal
sections.html:
A default is a safe value compiled into the app. A fetched value is a downloaded candidate. Activation makes fetched configuration visible through the SDK. Keep those states separate when a parameter could disrupt an ongoing editor, query or animation. The right activation moment is a product decision.

The optional source sets notes_page_size to a local default of 10 and tries fetchAndActivate. It returns ConfigSelection containing a validated page size and a separate diagnostic. Ordinary fetch failure still reads the active/default value; it reports retainedAfterFetchFailure without making notebook queries unavailable. Values from 1 through 25 are accepted. Missing, zero, negative or oversized inputs select 10. The rules still enforce their own upper limit of 25.

let absent = ConfigPolicy.pageSize(remote: nil) // 10
let small = ConfigPolicy.pageSize(remote: 5)    // 5
let huge = ConfigPolicy.pageSize(remote: 300)  // 10
// Apply the chosen size to a newly owned query.
// Do not reuse a cursor from a differently sized or filtered query.

Fetching can fail or be throttled. Preserve the default or last accepted configuration and explain the selected value in a non-sensitive diagnostic. Avoid zero minimum fetch intervals in a production polling loop. Real-time config updates also need a retained listener and activation policy; this lab does not implement that listener.

Use a staged rollout with an owner, a bounded cohort and recovery conditions. A kill switch may disable optional UI work, but it cannot retroactively undo a committed transaction or replace backend enforcement. Keep a local fallback for a malformed payload and a reviewed server rollback procedure for a bad published value.

ConfigPolicy.selection accepts only finite whole values from 1 through 25. Fractional, nonfinite and out-of-range values fall back to 10. A retained active value of 5 after fetch failure remains 5 with a failure diagnostic. Explicit cancellation throws CancellationError before or after the fetch; cancellation ends the owner's operation instead of publishing fallback data.

sections.title: Attestation complements identity and rules
sections.html:
Attestation is evidence about the app or device environment under a provider's contract. App Check can attach such evidence to supported backend requests. A valid App Check token does not identify Alice and does not grant rights to Bob's document. A valid Auth token likewise does not prove an unmodified client environment.

The real optional source implements AppCheckProviderFactory returning AppAttestProvider. It installs that factory before FirebaseApp.configure. In a later remote target, register the app with the appropriate provider in Firebase, configure Apple capabilities and the provider's environment as documented, then observe request metrics before enabling enforcement.

Debug providers support development where normal attestation is unavailable. Keep debug tokens outside commits and release targets, and revoke leaked test tokens. A simulator debug-provider success cannot prove physical-device App Attest behavior. Do not relax rules because an attestation check appears to work.

Define failure behavior for unavailable attestation, temporary outages and unsupported devices. Start with monitoring, verify expected client coverage, then enforce according to the reviewed product policy. The notebook's Auth/Firestore/Storage emulator target excludes App Check, so its local synthetic account flow is not an attestation test.

For this Firebase integration, set com.apple.developer.devicecheck.appattest-environment to production in the signed target's entitlements. Firebase App Check does not accept App Attest sandbox tokens. Inspect the built entitlement rather than relying on a capability checkbox. This setting does not establish successful physical-device attestation.

sections.title: A callable is an authenticated command boundary
sections.html:
A callable Function is a server endpoint with Firebase's callable request/response protocol. The client SDK can carry supported authentication and App Check evidence. The server must still validate request.auth, request data and product rights. An arbitrary HTTP function is not interchangeable with a callable without matching the protocol.

The supplied Swift requestCleanup sends mediaID, the upload receipt's generation string, and commandID to abandonMedia in us-central1. The server derives UID from request.auth rather than trusting an owner supplied by the client. It validates restricted ASCII IDs and accepts a command only under that caller's namespace.

A command ID distinguishes retries of one intended operation. Store the command payload with that ID. Repeating the same ID and payload returns the existing acceptance state; changing mediaID or generation under that command ID is a failed precondition. This prevents a retry identity from silently changing meaning.

Admin SDK operations bypass client security rules and instead depend on trusted server authority. Therefore the Function must perform its own ownership and input checks. App Check enforcement reduces one class of abuse but does not repair a Function that lets Alice choose Bob's UID or an arbitrary object path.

sections.title: Separate accepted work from completed work
sections.html:
The real Functions source writes a cleanup command transactionally, then returns accepted = true. Accepted means the durable job exists; it does not mean deletion is complete. A separate onDocumentCreated worker binds the original generation string, conditionally deletes the derived owned Storage path, and records the outcome before marking the job completed.

Deletion can succeed while marking the job completed fails. A retried worker keeps the original generation and applies the same deletion precondition. Missing original data is alreadyAbsent; a replacement is preserved on precondition failure. Progress records the outcome. Ordinary provider failures remain retryable rather than being recorded as completed.

Client rules deny all cleanupCommands paths; trusted Functions own them. The supplied source is a private-media cleanup example, not a deployed account-deletion workflow or a media-manifest engine. Published references require a coordinated invalidation policy. Cross-service cleanup still needs observability, bounded retries and support ownership.

Before a separately authorized local Functions test, provision compatible Functions/Admin SDK dependencies and a Functions emulator entry, point Admin Firestore and Storage to matching local services, and configure the demo bucket. The README specifies the gates and remaining integration. No installation, Function invocation or deployment occurred here.

A path alone cannot identify the intended stored version after deletion and recreation. The pure helper validates canonical positive generation strings and passes their exact digits to ifGenerationMatch. BigInt checks the integer range without producing an unsafe JavaScript Number. Synthetic tests use adjacent large generations to expose accidental rounding and replay against a replacement.

Run the pure fixture with node --test Functions/cleanup-policy.test.mjs from the lab directory. Its fake object store checks deletion preconditions and controlled replay schedules. It imports no Firebase/Admin/GCS SDK, executes no rules and proves no provider behavior. The actual conditional-delete API and error codes remain separately provisioned integration checks.

sections.title: Choose Realtime Database for connection-aware presence
sections.html:
Presence means an observed connection state, not proof that a person is reading a screen. Realtime Database provides .info/connected and server-registered onDisconnect actions. These are useful for a small connection-aware presence feature. Firestore listeners alone do not offer the same disconnect-registration mechanism.

Use a private presence/{uid}/{connectionID} entry for each installation or connection lifetime. Register onDisconnectRemoveValue and wait for registration success before writing online state with ServerValue.timestamp. If the network disappears, the server can remove that entry without a final client message.

One user's two connections need separate entries. A phone disconnecting should not mark an active tablet offline. Aggregate presence according to the product contract and account for the delay in detecting disconnects. Avoid promising immediate offline state or assuming a foreground app is proof of current human attention.

The optional PresenceOwner source observes connection state, registers removal, and advertises online. Its rules fixture permits only the owner account and validates online plus a server-time value. It is separate from the notebook's Firestore model. No Realtime Database emulator is included in the core emulator command.

sections.title: Own reconnect, signout and disconnect registrations
sections.html:
On reconnect, a connection owner must re-register its onDisconnect behavior before publishing online again. A previous connection's cleanup registration does not guarantee every future connection has one. Keep handles for .info/connected and remove the observer during teardown.

A signout can race with disconnect registration and its completion. The supplied adapter checks a local generation before advertising online. Its composition owner must call stop before replacing Auth credentials and verify removal acknowledgement and the old disconnect registration's lifetime under those credentials. This native lifecycle case remains an explicit independent exercise.

Realtime Database rules are a different language and data model from Firestore rules. Do not paste firestore.rules into database.rules.json. The fixture validates the private presence shape, denies extra children, and allows owner deletion; validation does not run on a deleted node. Plan direct unauthorized writes and stale-time cases for a separately gated rules run.

Optional later reading: lessons 091 and 108 deepen controlled clocks and operational adoption after this stage. exercise.solution:
Give the presence owner a generation that increments on start, stop and account replacement. Registration captures that generation and the account stamp. On completion, compare both before advertising online. Stopping removes the connection observer and arranges cleanup of the old connection under the chosen credential policy. Cancelling the observer alone cannot invalidate a completion already queued.

For cleanup, c1 with p1 writes one pending job under Alice's namespace. Retrying c1 with p1 reuses the job. Reusing c1 with p2 is a failed precondition. A worker binds p1's original generation g1 and uses a generation-match deletion precondition. Replay reconciles an absent original or preserves a replacement g2. Reuse of c1 with another generation is a failed precondition; no unsafe Number conversion is allowed.

Remote page size 300 falls back to 10, which stays below the list-rule maximum of 25. This is client validation, not authorization. App Check metrics, debug/physical device coverage, provider outages and supported-client adoption determine a staged enforcement decision; do not enable enforcement from a syntax check.

The RTDB plan includes owner create/delete, anonymous and cross-account denial, extra-child rejection and reconnect cleanup. The supplied database rules have not run in an interpreter. Your generation helper and eventual native/RTDB evidence are independent work rather than a completed production presence implementation.

For failed configuration fetch, return the validated active/default page size plus retainedAfterFetchFailure. Treat explicit task cancellation as cancellation. The remote target's signed App Attest entitlement must use production; simulator/debug-provider checks do not validate physical-device attestation.

lessons.title: Test authorization and hand off a recoverable Firebase feature
lessons.summary: Run the correct verification gates, review failures and cost exposure, assess an SDK upgrade, and produce a defensible integration handoff.
objectives: Distinguish host policy checks from actual Firebase rules execution.
Design adversarial authorization fixtures and a recovery matrix.
Estimate a bounded synthetic workload without inventing Firebase prices.
Review upgrades with sourced compatibility and provider evidence.
Name operational owners, rollout criteria and pending checks.

sections.title: State exactly what each check establishes
sections.html:
Verification is evidence that a particular behavior met a stated expectation under a stated environment. The test's name should reveal that environment. An offline policy check, a rules interpreter fixture, an SDK build, a simulator interaction and a remote provider observation are different checks with different conclusions.

The author compiled the two Host files in Swift 6 mode and executed 55 policy checks. The Swift adapter sources passed syntax-only parsing; Node fixtures and Functions source passed node --check. These results support the declared host behaviors and parseable syntax. They do not validate Firebase signatures, rules semantics or actual service behavior.

The SDK sources require a distinct iOS target and compile condition. The rules fixtures require provisioned Node modules and local Auth/Firestore/Storage emulator binaries. The optional operational services require another target/configuration and remote integration. A passing local build still would not prove APNs delivery or physical-device attestation.

Use a table with expected behavior, command, toolchain, observed result and remaining limit. Mark a pending row honestly rather than calling it pass because source exists. A future reviewer must be able to tell whether the rules engine ever evaluated the authorization expressions.

The corrected companion executes 55 Swift host policy checks and eight pure Node cleanup schedules. These test publication gates, create reconciliation, recovery boundaries and generation-preserving orchestration. Neither run imports Firebase modules or executes security rules. The original 30-check author baseline is historical evidence; use current output for the updated source.

sections.title: Try forbidden requests directly
sections.html:
An adversarial fixture sends an input that a friendly UI would normally reject. That is essential for security because a modified client can bypass local validation. The supplied rules fixtures import rules-unit-testing and Firebase's client APIs, create named authenticated contexts, and issue requests against the emulator.

initializeTestEnvironment loads the actual Firestore and Storage rule text. authenticatedContext supplies mocked token identity, and unauthenticatedContext supplies no identity. These contexts do not authenticate real accounts, but their requests execute the configured rules interpreter. assertFails and assertSucceeds compare the service result with the fixture expectation.

Firestore cases cover owner CRUD, anonymous and Bob reads, forged owner, extra keys, wrong types, invalid sizes, client timestamp, skipped or stale revisions, ownership transfer, unknown paths and list bounds. Storage cases cover owner get/delete, cross-account and anonymous access, MIME, metadata, zero/excess/exact-boundary bytes and forbidden overwrite.

beforeEach clears Firestore and Storage state; after cleans up the environment. Isolation prevents a prior fixture's object from turning a create into an update unexpectedly. Keep all submitted data synthetic. The fixture's three bytes marked JPEG intentionally test declarations rather than valid image rendering.

sections.title: Provision first, then execute the local suite
sections.html:
Provisioning means arranging the required tools and dependencies before a test starts. Under this assignment, dependencies and missing emulator binaries must not be downloaded. A Firebase CLI executable existing on disk is insufficient: startup may fetch an emulator jar, and Node imports may fail if their packages are missing.

Once a separately authorized environment has compatible binaries and modules already available, change to FirebaseProject/Emulator and run the exact gated README command. It selects demo-firebase-course, auth/firestore/storage only, and the local config. Environment assertions require the explicit gate and expected loopback endpoints.

The Firebase CLI sets relevant emulator endpoints for the command it executes. The fixture validates those values before initializing the suite. A wrong host or missing gate should fail visibly rather than falling through to a real backend. There is no production fallback, login command or deploy command in the lab workflow.

Official emulator documentation notes differences from production transactions, index enforcement and service limits. Java runtime requirements are also evolving; the evidence ledger cites the documented Java 21 migration notice rather than inventing a installed version. Record the exact provisioned CLI, Java, Node and package releases when actually running the suite.

sections.title: Name every partial success and its next owner
sections.html:
A recovery matrix maps an interrupted state to a safe next action. For an ambiguous create, preserve the draft ID and read that identity before retrying. For stale revision, preserve the edit and compare with the newer document. For listener failure, release or replace registration under a bounded retry policy.

For media uploaded without publication, retry the manifest or remove the abandoned orphan. For a token detachment with lost acknowledgement, retain a durable idempotent registry effect or reconcile the authoritative association. For account deletion, keep a trusted cleanup job with progress rather than treating local screen clearing as completion.

Include corrupted backend fields, cancelled tasks with late success, a late error after a newer success, same-UID relogin and unexpected permission denial. Account-owned requests carry a stamp. Before publishing after await or a callback hop, recheck ownership even if cancellation was requested.

A process restart is a different failure boundary from an in-memory schedule. Our host models hold state in memory; they do not prove atomic disk persistence or replay. A durable implementation must persist command intent, recover without duplicating effects and test restart between each external effect and its acknowledgement.

Add abandonment before any upload, dangling manifest repair, and delayed cleanup after path recreation. Record the original generation in durable cleanup intent. The pure replay fixture adds synthetic evidence only; native upload metadata and real generation-match deletion still need their own SDK/provider observations.

sections.title: Bound workload before estimating money
sections.html:
A quota is a service limit on a resource or operation. Cost is money charged under a product's pricing model. An emulator passing does not establish either. Check current official usage and pricing documents for the selected Firebase products, edition, region and plan before a real rollout.

Bound notebook queries, listener count, upload bytes, retry rate and cleanup batch size. Keep a small number of listeners under named owners and remove them when no longer useful. A leaked listener or a broad reconnect can produce work long after the user leaves the screen.

Use synthetic arithmetic to reason about workload without claiming a bill. If 100 sessions each read three ten-note pages, the simplified estimate is 100 × 3 × 10 = 3000 document appearances. It omits reconnects, empty queries, index-entry billing, rule-dependent reads, writes, storage and egress; it is not an exact Firestore billing calculator.

let reads = ConfigPolicy.readEstimate(
    sessions: 100, pageSize: 10, pages: 3
)
// Optional(3000): a synthetic workload estimate.
// Invalid sizes or arithmetic overflow return nil.

Set budget alerts, usage monitoring and operational thresholds in an eventual remote project. Firebase documents that a budget alert is not a hard spending cap. Name who responds, what optional workload can be disabled, and how critical user operations remain recoverable. Do not fabricate currency values or promise that a rules limit alone prevents every abuse cost.

For remote Storage, include the current Blaze billing prerequisite in the setup decision. Read the selected bucket's actual configuration and pricing, rather than treating the demo bucket name or a no-cost usage allowance as proof of free access. This course performs no billing-account linkage.

sections.title: Treat an SDK upgrade as a compatibility change
sections.html:
An SDK upgrade changes a dependency graph and sometimes platform requirements, APIs, initialization or runtime behavior. Read official release notes for both the current and candidate releases. Record the compiler, Swift package tools requirement, Xcode support, deployment targets and transitive dependencies. A latest label is not a test plan.

The evidence ledger cites the inspected Firebase 13.0.0 compatibility entry and the observed release-note page, while making no downloaded-version claim. Recheck the exact release chosen later. GoogleSignIn compatibility, App Check provider support and Functions/Admin runtime requirements are separate decisions; a Firebase package resolving does not prove them.

Run host contracts first, then rule fixtures with the same intended policies, then typecheck/build the isolated iOS target. Exercise Auth restoration and signout, Firestore transaction conflict and metadata, Storage cancellation/bounds, optional-service consent, and provider callbacks. Keep baseline and candidate evidence for comparison.

A binary rollback cannot necessarily undo a server schema/rules change or erase queued writes from newer clients. Use compatible readers and rules during adoption, gate new writes, and retain an old-client acceptance matrix. Optional later reading: lessons 044, 105 and 106 deepen graph and release-artifact review after this stage.

sections.title: Leave an auditable handoff with unresolved rows
sections.html:
A handoff names the next owner of work, not merely a collection of source files. Assign owners for rules review, identity/provider configuration, device delivery, cleanup jobs, consent, symbols, quotas and incident response. Write the rollback trigger and the safe reduced-function behavior for each external dependency.

Use acceptance evidence that someone else can reproduce: exact host command and output count, fixture command and rules digest when run, target/source list and resolved SDK graph, device/provider observations, and retained binary/symbol identifiers. Never include secret keys or raw tokens in that report.

List deliberate boundaries: no account authentication, console configuration, SDK download, emulator execution, target typecheck, simulator interaction, real image rendering, APNs send, telemetry upload, App Check validation, Function invocation or RTDB runtime occurred during authoring. These are pending integration tasks rather than failures hidden behind a host pass.

The original notebook teaches the full assigned Firebase sequence through concrete mechanisms and operational plans. It is not a claim to reproduce paid course material or to exhaust every Firebase product. Keep the learner's independent modifications and evidence pending; supplying a worked answer does not complete their practice.

Your added controlled case gets a separate result and description, so it is not mixed into the baseline count. Use pending rows for rule interpreter, SDK typecheck/build, simulator interaction, real providers and optional operational services. Each row names its required provisioned runtime or target and an acceptance behavior. For example, rules execution requires the gated Node command and must deny Bob's direct request to Alice's path, not merely hide a UI button.

An upgrade proposal cites current and candidate release requirements, selected product graph, provider compatibility and retained evidence. It plans compatible backend readers/rules before new writes, a bounded adoption cohort and an owner who can disable optional workload. Rolling back the binary is one action in a larger recovery plan.

This worked handoff explains the evidence shape. It does not manufacture a completed rules run, approved upgrade or learner submission. Retain your independently changed policy, command, observation and limitations for review.

Record the eight pure cleanup schedules separately from the 55 host policy checks. A fake precondition-aware store establishes the orchestrator's intent under controlled inputs, including large adjacent generation strings. It cannot establish that the selected Storage SDK honors the request, that an emulator implements those semantics, or that a remote service returned the expected status.
